scientific_interest.instructions: Assuming the measurements are valid, how much would planetary scientists want to study this detected Mars surface environmental event?

criteria.none: Ordinary day-to-day behaviour; nothing a scientist would look at twice
criteria.low: Slightly unusual, but within the range routinely seen at this site
criteria.medium: Clearly unusual and worth a record, but of a kind seen fairly often
criteria.high: A strong, rare, long-lasting or multi-sensor departure from usual conditions that scientists would study
criteria.exceptional: Among the most unusual environmental events this instrument records, e.g. a major solar particle event or an extreme atmospheric event

phenomenon_class.instructions: Which kind of natural phenomenon best explains this event, assuming the measurements are valid?

criteria.atmospheric: A change in the atmosphere: pressure, dust, humidity or ultraviolet flux
criteria.radiation: A change in the surface radiation environment measured by the dosimeter
criteria.thermal: A change in air or ground temperature not explained by the usual daily cycle
criteria.other_physical: A real physical change that fits none of the classes above
criteria.uncertain: The description does not clearly point to one of these classes

radiation dose rate (detector E).pattern: brief decrease relative to the usual value at this local time

scientific_interest.instructions: Assuming the measurements are valid, how much would planetary scientists want to study this detected Mars surface environmental event?

criteria.none: Ordinary day-to-day behaviour; nothing a scientist would look at twice
criteria.low: Slightly unusual, but within the range routinely seen at this site
criteria.medium: Clearly unusual and worth a record, but of a kind seen fairly often
criteria.high: A strong, rare, long-lasting or multi-sensor departure from usual conditions that scientists would study
criteria.exceptional: Among the most unusual environmental events this instrument records, e.g. a major solar particle event or an extreme atmospheric event

phenomenon_class.instructions: Which kind of natural phenomenon best explains this event, assuming the measurements are valid?

criteria.atmospheric: A change in the atmosphere: pressure, dust, humidity or ultraviolet flux
criteria.radiation: A change in the surface radiation environment measured by the dosimeter
criteria.thermal: A change in air or ground temperature not explained by the usual daily cycle
criteria.other_physical: A real physical change that fits none of the classes above
criteria.uncertain: The description does not clearly point to one of these classes

radiation dose rate (detector B).pattern: sustained increase relative to the usual value at this local time

radiation dose rate (detector E).pattern: sustained increase relative to the usual value at this local time
radiation dose rate (detector E).magnitude: extreme relative to the local baseline
